title: AI News Radar
description: Real-time panoramic intelligence radar for global frontier AI breakthroughs.

items.title: Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI
items.content_text: Gilbert + Tobin, a premier Australian law firm, has fully integrated AI into its legal documentation and research processes to tackle increasing workloads. By automating manual legal tasks, the firm aims to optimize service efficiency and cost structures while maintaining high legal standards.

items.title: An analysis of the tech job market in late 2026: product managers seem to be benefiting most in the AI era, demand for engineers is plateauing, and more (Lenny Rachitsky/Lenny's Newsletter)
items.content_text: A late-2026 analysis of the global tech job market reveals that while hiring is growing, the focus has shifted from pure software engineering to product management. With AI automating basic coding tasks, professionals capable of driving cross-functional collaboration and business outcomes are now the most sought-after assets.

items.title: Sources: Anthropic's bankers are weighing plans to raise its IPO price following heavy demand, which could increase the valuation target to $1.5T or more (Financial Times)
items.content_text: Due to overwhelming market demand, investment banks are considering a significant hike in Anthropic's IPO price. A valuation potentially exceeding $1.5 trillion would challenge current Silicon Valley norms, signaling that the investor frenzy for AI-native infrastructure is entering a fever pitch.

items.title: A deep dive into AMD's Zen 6 EPYC Venice: it uses TSMC's N2P, the 9686F often beats Nvidia's Vera, a dual 9996 is up to 93% faster than a dual Zen 5 9965, more (Jake Roach/Tom's Hardware)
items.content_text: Details of AMD's Zen 6 architecture have emerged, featuring the TSMC N2P node and significant redesigns including a new vector engine, native FP16 support, and a dual IOD configuration. With CCDs now scaling up to 12 cores for standard and 32 cores for dense variants, the architecture aims to drastically outperform its predecessor in throughput and density.

items.title: NY-based Daylight, which provides AI-powered managed security, raised an $80M Series B led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives, sources say at a ~$400M valuation (Maria Armental/Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: New York-based AI security startup Daylight raised $80 million in a Series B funding round led by Goldman Sachs Alternatives. This investment brings the company's valuation to approximately $400 million, aiming to scale its AI-driven managed security services for enterprise protection.

items.title: In a report, Railway says it believes the October hack targeted AI provider keys for resale, and unauthorized spend on the stolen keys was estimated at ~$740K (Lawrence Abrams/BleepingComputer)
items.content_text: Cloud provider Railway suffered a breach in October where hackers exploited vulnerabilities to steal AI provider API keys. The stolen keys were subsequently resold or used for unauthorized operations, resulting in approximately $740,000 in fraudulent charges.

items.title: Leaked documents: OpenAI's adjusted operating margin improved from -150% to -109% from Q2 to Q3 (Berber Jin/Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: Leaked internal documents indicate OpenAI's adjusted operating margin improved from -150% to -109% between Q2 and Q3. This shift reflects the company's efforts to balance massive infrastructure and talent spending with rapid revenue growth to offset operational costs.

items.title: Leaked documents: OpenAI's adjusted operating margin improved from -150% to -109% from Q2 to Q3 (Berber Jin/Wall Street Journal)
items.content_text: Leaked documents reveal that OpenAI's adjusted operating margin improved from -150% in Q2 to -109% in Q3. Despite significant revenue growth, the company remains deep in the red due to massive compute costs, leaving profitability as a distant goal.

items.title: CoreWeave reports Q3 revenue up 168% YoY to $3.66B, vs. $3.55B est., a net loss of $709M, and a $132.5B revenue backlog, up from $104B as of June (Jordan Novet/CNBC)
items.content_text: CoreWeave reported a 168% YoY revenue increase to $3.66B in its latest quarterly report, and despite a $709M net loss, it raised its 2026 revenue guidance supported by a massive $132.5B backlog. This move aims to assure the market that demand for its GPU-rental services remains robust amid industry volatility.

items.title: Sources: the US Commerce Dept. delayed new Entity List additions for two months, leaving off Megaspeed despite four other US agencies pushing for its inclusion (Financial Times)
items.content_text: The U.S. Commerce Department has delayed adding new companies to its Entity List by two months, despite pressure from four other agencies. Notably, Megaspeed, a company linked to the recent controversy involving NVIDIA’s leadership, was omitted, highlighting the subtle balancing act of trade sanctions amidst complex geopolitical interests.

items.title: Source: OpenAI told investors on Tuesday that its revenue jumped 50% to around $10B in Q3, up from 17% growth in Q2 (The Information)
items.content_text: OpenAI disclosed to investors on Tuesday that its annualized revenue reached approximately $10 billion in Q3, with the growth rate surging from 17% in Q2 to 50%. This momentum is driven by the rapid scaling of enterprise services and paid user subscriptions, demonstrating a significant acceleration in commercial monetization.

items.title: Grok Build coding agent leaks oodles of confidential info, some belonging to SpaceXSI
items.content_text: The Grok Build platform by SpaceXSI has been exposed for a critical URL enumeration flaw, leading to the public leak of thousands of user apps and sensitive business data, including internal plans and employee information. Even SpaceXSI, the platform's own creator, saw its internal documents compromised, highlighting severe security oversight in its rapid development cycle.

items.title: S-1: Nvidia plans to invest about $10B in Anthropic after its IPO, or ~10% of the new cash Anthropic is expected to raise this month, including in the IPO (Cory Weinberg/New York Times)
items.content_text: Nvidia plans to invest approximately $10 billion into Anthropic during and after its IPO, accounting for roughly 10% of the total capital raised. This move is designed to lock the top-tier LLM developer into Nvidia's compute ecosystem and solidify its dominance in AI infrastructure.

items.title: Graphon, which wants to resolve AI agent memory limitations by mapping connections across documents, videos, and images, raised a $35M Series A (Shubhangi Goel/Business Insider)
items.content_text: Graphon, based in San Francisco, raised $35 million in Series A funding to develop software that maps connections between documents, videos, and images. CEO Arbaaz Khan aims to solve the AI agent memory fragmentation problem by creating a 'connected fabric' of information rather than isolated data snippets.

items.title: OpenAI turns ChatGPT into a business directory with AI agents that handle customer questions
items.content_text: OpenAI has launched a beta feature called 'Businesses in ChatGPT,' allowing merchants to manage product feeds, prices, and availability via a Business Hub. By enabling AI agents to answer customer queries directly within chats, OpenAI is effectively challenging Google's dominance in commercial search.

items.title: Lawsuit filing: Point72's quant unit Cubist claims its fired lead research analyst used Claude and Codex to steal source code before leaving for a competitor (Bloomberg)
items.content_text: Point72's quantitative unit, Cubist, has filed a lawsuit against a former lead research analyst, alleging that the employee used AI tools like Claude and Codex to steal proprietary source code before jumping to a competitor. This case highlights a new frontier in financial compliance: monitoring internal misuse of generative AI for intellectual property theft.

items.title: Lawsuit filing: Point72's quant unit Cubist claims its fired lead research analyst used Claude and Codex to steal source code before leaving for a competitor (Bloomberg)
items.content_text: Cubist, a quantitative trading unit of Point72, has filed a lawsuit accusing a former lead research analyst of using AI tools like Claude and Codex to steal proprietary source code before leaving for a competitor. This case marks a significant legal milestone in the financial sector regarding the use of generative AI in corporate espionage.

items.title: SpaceX announces Starlink Mini 2 with a swappable battery that it says can operate for over four hours without an external power source, reportedly for $999 (Andrew Liszewski/The Verge)
items.content_text: SpaceX has unveiled the Starlink Mini 2, an all-in-one satellite terminal featuring an integrated dish, Wi-Fi router, and a swappable battery. Thinner than its predecessor at 23.1mm, the device offers 4.5 hours of autonomy and is priced at $999, which includes a year of unlimited roaming service for mobile and off-grid users.

items.title: Clara, which sells corporate spend management tools in Latin America, raised $105M, including a $65M Series C and $40M in renewed growth financing (Maria Clara Cobo/Bloomberg)
items.content_text: São Paulo-based corporate spending startup Clara has raised $105 million, comprising a $65 million Series C round and $40 million in debt growth financing. The fresh capital will be used to scale its corporate expense management operations across Latin America.

items.title: Anthropic turns Claude into a full workspace with Plugins, spreadsheets, whiteboards, and soon Meeting notes
items.content_text: Anthropic has transformed Claude into a comprehensive workspace by introducing collaboration features such as AI-assisted spreadsheets, interactive whiteboards, and data dashboard integration with tools like Snowflake and Salesforce. A meeting assistant is also slated for imminent release to bolster enterprise productivity.

items.title: Google Fi launches "super network" for automatic carrier switching and Wi-Fi Auto-Connect+ to improve indoor connectivity in places like malls and airports (Sam Rutherford/Engadget)
items.content_text: It’s rolling out first on Pixel phones before wider availability arrives in 2027. Getting the fastest mobile data speeds can be tricky because a single carrier may not have optimal coverage in your area. So to address this, Google Fi is introducing its new super network feature which allows your phone to automatically switch between two different carriers to deliver the best connection possible. items.title: Nvidia's model GR00T 2 watches humans on video, then imagines itself as the robot
items.content_text: To teach robots new tasks, humans usually have to laboriously teleoperate them during training. Nvidia's new AI model GR00T 2 is designed to cut that effort by transferring human movements from videos to robotic arms. To train a robot for new tasks, engineers usually spend hours remotely controlling the machines. This so-called teleoperation is expensive, slow, and needs its own data for every robot model.
